criteria: `parse_env(text)` in `envfile.py` reads `KEY=value` lines and returns a `dict` that maps `str` keys to `str` values.
`parse_env` treats each setting as one line of the form `KEY=value`. The line is split at the first `=` and any later `=` belongs to the value: `TOKEN=abc=def` gives `{"TOKEN": "abc=def"}`.
`parse_env` drops whitespace around the key and around the value: `parse_env("  A = 1  ")` is `{"A": "1"}`. An empty value is allowed: `A=` gives `{"A": ""}`.

`parse_env` skips a line that is empty or only whitespace. It skips a line whose first non-whitespace character is `#` as a comment, so a commented line such as `# database` does not become a setting. A `#` anywhere else is part of the value: `COLOR=#fff` gives `{"COLOR": "#fff"}`.

In `parse_env`, when the trimmed value is at least two characters long and starts and ends with the same quote character, `"` or `'`, that pair of quotes is removed: `NAME="my app"` gives `{"NAME": "my app"}`. Whitespace inside the quotes is kept: `parse_env('PAD=" x "')` is `{"PAD": " x "}`.

`parse_env` removes only one pair of quotes: `parse_env('A=""x""')` is `{"A": '"x"'}`. Quotes that do not match are kept as written: `parse_env('B="x\'')` is `{"B": '"x\''}` and `parse_env('C="x')` is `{"C": '"x'}`. A value that is one quote character on its own is kept too: `parse_env('D="')` is `{"D": '"'}`.
In `parse_env`, a key that is set more than once takes its last value.
`parse_env` raises `ValueError` for a line that is not blank and not a comment when the line has no `=` or when its key is empty, as in `=5`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
